svg.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Mechanics, Edge Cases & Mathematical Invariants
svg.desc: Visual comparison of all five classic rate limiting algorithms (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, Fixed Window Counter with 2x boundary burst flaw, Sliding Window Log, Sliding Window Counter) plus the Generic Cell Rate Algorithm (GCRA) showing Theoretical Arrival Time (TAT), state footprints, and mathematical admission invariants.
svg.text: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Mechanics, Edge Cases & Mathematical Invariants
Token Bucket · Leaky Bucket · Fixed Window Counter & 2× Boundary Flaw · Sliding Window Log · Sliding Window Counter · GCRA (TAT)
1. Token Bucket (Capacity B, Refill Rate R)
Admissions over interval s ≤ B + R·s · Instantaneous burst capped at B
State per key: { tokens: float64, last_refill_ms: int64 } (16 bytes) · O(1) time & space
Standard: AWS API Gateway, Envoy Token Bucket, Stripe Request Rate Limiter
Tolerates client traffic bursts while bounding long-term average rate to R.
2. Leaky Bucket (FIFO Queue, Strict Outflow Rate R)
Outflow rate strictly ≤ R · Queue delay for arrival i = (queue_depth_i) / R
State per key: { water_level: int, last_leak_ms: int64 } or FIFO queue · O(1) / O(B)
Standard: uber-go/ratelimit, network egress traffic shaping (policing vs shaping)
Critical downside: Recent requests delayed behind stale queue backlog.
3. Fixed Window Counter & 2× Boundary Burst Flaw
BOUNDARY FLAW: 200 requests admitted inside Δt = 200 ms (2× limit!)
For any ε > 0, L reqs @ (W-ε) and L reqs @ (W+ε) yields 2L admissions in 2ε.
Invariant holds ONLY per discrete calendar window, NOT across sliding windows!
State: { window_id: int64, counter: int } (12 bytes) · Memory: O(1) · Time: O(1)
Danger: Never use as sole protection for downstream capacity bounds.
4. Sliding Window Log (Exact Rolling Window [t - W, t])
Exact Timestamp Log in Redis Sorted Set (ZSET)
2. ZCARD key -- Count; if < L then ZADD key now now & admit
Admissions in [t - W, t] strictly ≤ L · Absolutely zero boundary burst flaw
Memory: O(L) per key (1M keys @ 1k limit = ~8 GB RAM) · Time: O(log L + M)
Best for: High-value, low-limit auth routes (brute-force defense, login, payments).
Estimated Count: ĉ = c_prev · (1 - e / W) + c_cur
Error bounded by c_prev · min(e/W, 1 - e/W) · Assumes uniform prior distribution
State per key: { c_prev: int, c_cur: int, window_start: int64 } (16 bytes) · O(1) space & time
Industry Standard: Cloudflare edge rate limiter, GitHub API sliding counter.
6. GCRA (Theoretical Arrival Time — Single-Timestamp Leaky Bucket)
Parameters: Emission T = 1/R · Burst Tolerance τ = (B - 1)·T
if t < TAT - τ: REJECT (retryAfter = (TAT - τ) - t) -- Bucket empty
else: ADMIT and update TAT = max(t, TAT) + T -- One atomic Redis SET!
Exact Token Bucket semantics with ZERO background timers and ZERO race conditions!
State per key: Exactly 1 timestamp (int64 TAT = 8 bytes) · Memory: O(1) · Time: O(1)
Origin: ATM Forum TM 4.0 / UNI 3.1 · Modern standard: Brandur Leach / redis-cell / Valkey
